_meta.name: Optimizations
_meta.description: Four-phase sprint implementing the Optimizations project from the roadmap. Phase 1 (scripts directory reorganization) and Phase 2 (shared naming helper) are substantially complete based on the current state of the repository — directories exist, READMEs are in place, and naming_utils.py is deployed in scripts/utilities/. The sprint tasks for those phases serve as verification checkpoints. Phases 3 and 4 (metadata population upstream and DOMAIN_PATTERNS hybrid approach) are the primary implementation targets.

progress_keys.blocked_by: task id or external dependency that prevents progress
progress_keys.completed_at: ISO 8601 date when status flipped to complete

session_variances.intent: Ship the four sub-tasks of the Optimizations roadmap item. Do not expand scope. Do not refactor callers outside the specified modules.
session_variances.phase_1_note: Directory structure and READMEs for data_processing/, template_management/, orchestration/, utilities/ appear to already exist. Scripts appear already moved. Phase 1 tasks are verification gates — if they pass on inspection, mark complete immediately.
session_variances.phase_2_note: naming_utils.py exists at scripts/utilities/naming_utils.py with sanitize_for_filename, build_dated_artifact_path, and derive_basename_from_job_json. Verify batch-process.sh and py_orchestrate_correlation_to_pdf.py are calling it rather than duplicating logic.
session_variances.phase_4_note: DOMAIN_PATTERNS refactor is the highest-risk change. Implement the loader without removing the inline fallback dict until the loader is verified working.

phases.name: Scripts directory reorganization verification
phases.goal: Confirm that the scripts/ directory structure is fully in place and all scripts run from their new locations.

tasks.title: Verify directory structure and READMEs exist
tasks.what: Confirm data_processing/, template_management/, orchestration/, and utilities/ each exist and contain a README.md.
tasks.how: ls scripts/data_processing/README.md scripts/template_management/README.md scripts/orchestration/README.md scripts/utilities/README.md — all four must exist.
tasks.done_when: All four README.md files exist. If any are missing, create a brief README describing the directory's purpose and contents.
tasks.notes: Based on current repo state, these appear to already exist. Mark complete immediately if confirmed.

tasks.title: Verify scripts are in correct subdirectories
tasks.what: Confirm each script is in its target subdirectory: data_processing/ contains py_skill_job_correlator.py and extract-html-data.js; orchestration/ contains batch-process.sh and py_orchestrate_correlation_to_pdf.py; template_management/ contains py_adapter_correlator_to_template.py; utilities/ contains naming_utils.py, sanitize.js, debug-sanitize.js, config_manager.py.
tasks.done_when: All expected files present in their target directories. If any are missing, move them with `mv <source> <target>` and update any hardcoded paths inside the moved file.
tasks.notes: Also confirm that the root scripts/ directory no longer contains any of the original files (they should only live in subdirectories now).

tasks.title: Smoke-test scripts from their new locations
tasks.what: Run each moved Python script with --help or a dry-run mode to confirm no import errors from path changes.

steps: python scripts/data_processing/py_skill_job_correlator.py --help 2>&1 | head -5
python scripts/orchestration/py_orchestrate_correlation_to_pdf.py --help 2>&1 | head -5
python scripts/template_management/py_adapter_correlator_to_template.py --help 2>&1 | head -5
python scripts/utilities/naming_utils.py sanitize 'Test Company Software Engineer' -- should print 'Test-Company-Software-Engineer'

tasks.done_when: Each script runs without ImportError or FileNotFoundError. naming_utils.py CLI mode returns a sanitized string.
tasks.notes: Path-relative imports (e.g. SKILLS_INDEX_PATH = _SCRIPT_DIR.parent.parent / 'skills-index.json') may need updating after moves — check each file.

phases.name: Shared naming helper integration
phases.goal: Ensure batch-process.sh and py_orchestrate_correlation_to_pdf.py both delegate filename sanitization to naming_utils.py and produce identical output.

tasks.title: Verify batch-process.sh calls naming_utils.py for filename construction
tasks.what: Confirm batch-process.sh calls naming_utils.py (not sanitize.js or inline awk/sed) for any filename sanitization steps.
tasks.how: grep -n 'naming_utils\|sanitize\|sed\|awk' scripts/orchestration/batch-process.sh — look for any filename construction that is not delegating to naming_utils.py.
tasks.done_when: batch-process.sh has no inline filename sanitization logic. Any sanitize step calls `python scripts/utilities/naming_utils.py <company> <title>` or equivalent.
tasks.notes: If batch-process.sh still calls sanitize.js or has inline logic, replace those calls with: `BASE_NAME=$(python "$script_dir/../utilities/naming_utils.py" "$COMPANY" "$TITLE")`

tasks.title: Verify py_orchestrate_correlation_to_pdf.py imports naming_utils
tasks.what: Confirm py_orchestrate_correlation_to_pdf.py imports and uses sanitize_for_filename or build_dated_artifact_path from naming_utils rather than re-implementing filename logic.
tasks.done_when: py_orchestrate_correlation_to_pdf.py imports from naming_utils (e.g. `from scripts.utilities.naming_utils import sanitize_for_filename, build_dated_artifact_path` or via sys.path insert) and does not have a local copy of sanitization logic.
tasks.notes: Use sys.path manipulation if the module is not on the Python path: `sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent / 'utilities'))` then `from naming_utils import sanitize_for_filename`.

tasks.title: Test filename consistency between batch-process.sh and py_orchestrate_correlation_to_pdf.py
tasks.what: Run both scripts against the same input and confirm the output filename is identical.

steps: 1. Pick a sample job JSON from the queue.
2. Run batch-process.sh in --dry-run mode and capture the proposed output filename.
3. Run py_orchestrate_correlation_to_pdf.py in --dry-run mode against the same input and capture its proposed filename.
4. Assert both filenames are equal.

tasks.done_when: Both scripts produce the same sanitized filename for the same input. Any discrepancy is resolved by aligning both to naming_utils.py output.
tasks.notes: If --dry-run is not supported, add a temporary print statement to surface the proposed filename without writing files.

phases.name: Metadata population upstream
phases.goal: Update py_skill_job_correlator.py to extract job_title and employer from job posting data and populate metadata fields before correlation, then use those fields in filename generation.

tasks.title: Locate and read job posting JSON structure
tasks.what: Understand what keys are available in the job posting JSON input that correlator receives, specifically where job title and employer/company name live.

steps: 1. Find where the job JSON is loaded in py_skill_job_correlator.py: grep -n 'json.load\|open.*json\|job_data\|posting' scripts/data_processing/py_skill_job_correlator.py
2. Print one sample job JSON to understand its structure: python -c "import json; d=json.load(open('<sample_job_json_path>')); print(json.dumps(d, indent=2))" | head -40
3. Identify the key names for: job title (likely 'title', 'job_title', or 'position'), employer (likely 'company', 'employer', 'organization').

tasks.done_when: Key names for job_title and employer confirmed. p3_t2 can reference them.
tasks.notes: The extract-html-data.js output (the preprocess-batch-export-resume.json) likely defines the schema. Check that file for the available fields.

tasks.title: Extract and populate metadata.job_title and metadata.employer in correlator output
tasks.what: Modify py_skill_job_correlator.py to read job_title and employer from the input job posting data and write them into the output correlation JSON under a 'metadata' key before any correlation logic runs.

steps: 1. After loading the job posting JSON, extract: `job_title = job_data.get('<title_key>', '')` and `employer = job_data.get('<employer_key>', '')`.
2. Ensure the output dict has a 'metadata' sub-dict: `output.setdefault('metadata', {})['job_title'] = job_title` and `output['metadata']['employer'] = employer`.
3. Place this extraction BEFORE the skill correlation loop so that metadata is available even if correlation fails partially.
4. Verify the metadata key appears in the output JSON by running correlator on a sample and inspecting the result.

tasks.done_when: Running py_skill_job_correlator.py on a sample job JSON produces output with metadata.job_title and metadata.employer populated with non-empty values. Confirmed by: `python scripts/data_processing/py_skill_job_correlator.py <sample> | python -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['metadata']['job_title'], d['metadata']['employer'])"`
tasks.notes: Do not remove any existing metadata fields — only add job_title and employer. Other callers (py_adapter_correlator_to_template.py) may read metadata and should not be broken.

tasks.title: Update filename generation to use metadata.job_title and metadata.employer
tasks.what: Wherever the output PDF or artifact filename is constructed, replace any hardcoded or path-derived name with: `naming_utils.py <employer> <job_title>` (via shell) or `sanitize_for_filename(f'{employer} {job_title}')` (via Python), reading the values from the correlation JSON's metadata fields.

how.shell_pattern: In batch-process.sh: after running py_skill_job_correlator.py, parse the output JSON to extract employer and job_title, then call: `BASE_NAME=$(python "$script_dir/../utilities/naming_utils.py" "$employer" "$job_title")`

tasks.done_when: A run through the full pipeline produces a PDF/artifact named using the actual employer and job title extracted from the posting (e.g. 'Shopify-Senior-Backend-Engineer-2026-05-10.pdf'), not a generic or path-derived name.
tasks.notes: Add a fallback: if metadata.employer and metadata.job_title are both empty, fall back to derive_basename_from_job_json(job_json_path) to maintain backward compatibility.

phases.name: DOMAIN_PATTERNS hybrid approach
phases.goal: Reduce duplication between the hardcoded DOMAIN_PATTERNS dict in py_adapter_correlator_to_template.py and the role-based-templates directory by implementing a loader that reads domain metadata from template files, with an inline fallback.

tasks.title: Audit current DOMAIN_PATTERNS and role-based-templates for overlap
tasks.what: Map every domain in DOMAIN_PATTERNS (devops, backend, frontend, …) to its counterpart template file in role-based-templates/ and identify which data (keywords, highlights) is duplicated.

steps: 1. List template files: ls role-based-templates/
2. For each domain key in DOMAIN_PATTERNS, check if a matching template file exists: grep -l '<domain>' role-based-templates/*.html
3. Compare the 'keywords' and 'highlights' arrays in DOMAIN_PATTERNS with any structured data in the matching template file.
4. Document the overlap in a comment at the top of py_adapter_correlator_to_template.py before implementing the loader.

tasks.done_when: Overlap mapping complete. Decision made: which fields can be read from templates vs which must stay hardcoded (e.g. 'facet_types' which is Python-only).
tasks.notes: If role-based-templates/ files are HTML with no structured metadata section, Phase 4 may require adding a <script type='application/json'> block or a sidecar YAML file per template to carry machine-readable domain metadata.

tasks.title: Design and implement the hybrid loader
tasks.what: Implement load_domain_patterns(templates_dir: Path) -> dict that reads domain metadata from template files (or sidecar files) and merges with the inline DOMAIN_PATTERNS dict as a fallback for domains with no template file.

how.approach: Sidecar YAML per template (preferred if templates are HTML). Each template gets a matching <domain>.yaml file in role-based-templates/ with keys: keywords (list[str]), highlights (list[str]). The loader reads each YAML, merges with DOMAIN_PATTERNS inline dict, with YAML taking precedence.
implementation: import yaml  # add to requirements if not present
# Merge: inline dict provides defaults for any domain without a yaml file, and for missing keys within a domain
merged = dict(DOMAIN_PATTERNS)  # start with full inline dict
merged[domain].update(data)  # YAML overrides inline for matching keys
how.call_site: Replace the direct reference to DOMAIN_PATTERNS with: `DOMAIN_PATTERNS = load_domain_patterns(Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / 'role-based-templates')`  at module load time.

tasks.done_when: py_adapter_correlator_to_template.py runs correctly with load_domain_patterns(); existing test runs (or manual invocation) produce identical domain-matching output as before the refactor. The inline DOMAIN_PATTERNS dict remains as the fallback (do not delete it).
tasks.notes: Do not require YAML files to exist — the loader must silently fall through to the inline dict if role-based-templates/ has no YAML files. This keeps the system portable without a full migration.

tasks.title: Create sidecar YAML files for existing template domains
tasks.what: For each domain in DOMAIN_PATTERNS that has a matching template file in role-based-templates/, create a <domain>.yaml sidecar containing the keywords and highlights arrays from the inline dict. This is the migration step that actually reduces duplication.

steps: 1. For each domain (devops, backend, frontend, etc.) that has a template in role-based-templates/:
Create role-based-templates/<domain>.yaml with content:
keywords: [list from inline DOMAIN_PATTERNS[domain]['keywords']]
highlights:
- "..first highlight.."
- "..second highlight.."
2. After creating YAML files, verify load_domain_patterns() loads them correctly.
3. Remove the corresponding inner dict from the inline DOMAIN_PATTERNS in py_adapter_correlator_to_template.py — leaving only domains that have no template file.

tasks.done_when: At least one domain's keywords and highlights are loaded exclusively from a sidecar YAML (not from the inline dict). The inline DOMAIN_PATTERNS dict is smaller than before. Adapter runs correctly.
tasks.notes: Migrate domains one at a time and run tests after each migration. Do not migrate all domains in a single step — if a YAML is malformed it will break everything.

tasks.title: Verify performance and portability
tasks.what: Confirm the hybrid approach does not noticeably increase startup time and works in environments where role-based-templates/ YAML files may not be present.

steps: 1. Time the script before and after: `time python scripts/template_management/py_adapter_correlator_to_template.py <sample_input> /dev/null`
2. Remove role-based-templates/*.yaml temporarily and verify the script still runs using the inline fallback.
3. Restore the YAML files.

tasks.done_when: Startup time overhead from YAML loading is < 100ms on the development machine. Script works with no YAML files present (inline fallback only).
tasks.notes: Cache the loaded patterns at module import time (not per-call) to avoid repeated disk I/O.
